session.assistantText:
Goal restated: this repo is an empty capability probe. The work is to run it with each delegated role bound to the route in the project role file `$DSH_HOME/pstack-models.json`, and to confirm the file is actually read before the run.

I read the role file and `pstack_roles` (which is the harness view of it) — both agree on every role, so the config is loaded.

Building one small deliverable: a lever that reads the role file and prints the role→route table, so the mapping is checkable rather than asserted.
Role file confirmed and read before dispatch. Now running the distinct configured routes for real, one child per role seat.
Review found real defects in the tool. Let me check the packaged reader's actual contract before fixing.
Real defects confirmed against the packaged reader contract. Delegating the fix on the bug-fix role route.
Now I verify independently rather than trusting the report.
The run used the project's role file, and the file was confirmed read before any delegation.

## Role file confirmation

`$DSH_HOME/pstack-models.json` (version 2) and the harness `pstack_roles` view agree on every role, so the config is live, not assumed. Both list these routes:

| Role | Provider | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| feature, refactoring | magpie | workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash | low |
| bug-fix | magpie | workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash | low |
| perf-issue | magpie | workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash | low |
| hillclimb | magpie | workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash | high |
| judgment and prose | magpie | workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash | high |
| arena runners (list) | deepseek-v4.1-flash / low, minimax-m3.1-flash / high | | |
| arena cross-judge pool (list) | minimax-m3.1-flash / high, deepseek-v4.1-flash / low | | |
| swarm workers (list) | deepseek-v4.1-flash / low, minimax-m3.1-flash / high | | |
| interrogate reviewers (list) | minimax-m3.1-flash / high, deepseek-v4.1-flash / low | | |

Every child I started was launched with exactly the route from its role line. Session transcripts confirm the requests carried the configured provider, model, and effort.

## What each role did

- feature, refactoring built the tool, [rolefile.ts](rolefile.ts), which prints the role-to-route table.
- judgment and prose wrote [prose.md](prose.md).
- arena runners (deepseek seat) wrote the alternative parser sketch, [arena-runner.md](arena-runner.md).
- interrogate reviewers (minimax seat) wrote [review-notes.md](review-notes.md), which found nine real defects in the first parser.
- swarm workers (deepseek seat) wrote the verifier, [verify-rolefile.sh](verify-rolefile.sh).
- bug-fix repaired the parser against the packaged reader contract in `src/roles/`.

## The defects that mattered

The review found the original parser blind-cast the JSON, so a version-1 role file printed every role as blank, unknown and retired role keys printed as live rows, the inherit alias landed in the provider column, and a missing file crashed. The repaired parser now matches the packaged reader. Measured by me, not by the report: missing file exits 0 with the inherit message, bad version and invalid JSON exit 1 with a one-line error, an unknown key becomes an issue line, a retired key drops silently, and the alias prints in its own column.

One thing outside the workspace is worth knowing. `~/.dsh/pstack-models.json` exists too, is version 1, and uses a different effort budget. This session's `DSH_HOME` points elsewhere, so the sandboxed file was the one in effect.

## Verification

`./verify-rolefile.sh` prints PASS. The tool's live output matches the role file exactly, and the [version-1 fixture](fixtures/version-1.json) prints real providers and models.

Nothing was committed and no git remote exists.
Delivered. The role file was read before dispatch, every subagent ran on its configured route, and the parser was repaired against the packaged reader contract with the negative paths verified by me directly.
